app.privacyBody:
Site. Static site on GitHub Pages, without cookies and without analytics. When the page is requested, GitHub processes technically necessary data such as the IP address (GitHub privacy statement). The browser also loads map tiles (OpenStreetMap), the operators' open vehicle feeds and, in operations, routes (OSRM/FOSSGIS), addresses (Nominatim) and surroundings (Overpass); these services see the IP address. The browser stores language and view locally.

Data. The analysis uses the sharing operators' open vehicle data (GBFS): location, charge and availability of vehicles, nothing about riders. The collector processes vehicle IDs only internally (keyed hash with a private key, HMAC) and deletes them at the latest 24 h after a vehicle has disappeared; they are not published. Published are totals per municipality, operator and hour (per hour only 0 or at least 3 events, smaller amounts in an hour of the same time-of-day band) and per cell (cell × time-of-day band only from {cellMin} events), origin-destination pairs only from {flowMin} trips per day, and the latest fleet without IDs, with idle time only in classes (under 6 h, 6–24 h, whole days).

Purpose and retention. Analysis of the sharing supply (fleet, use, forecast). Where the derived data could relate to persons: legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). Events and flows 30 days, cells 14 days, daily values per municipality and operator in the archive without limit, the live fleet only for the latest run.

In full: privacy policy (English version at the end).

Contact. Via the project's issues: github.com/fcou1005/mobility-pulse.

app.availableMeansBookableNot: Available means bookable: not reserved, not disabled. For stations, physical stock, bookable stock (is_installed and is_renting) and return docks are kept separate; a closed station does not count its vehicles as available. Station-based sources are added to the vehicle fleet only if the source provides no vehicle list.
app.collectorRatesEveryFeed: The collector rates every feed during the run: up to five minutes old current, up to 30 minutes delayed, beyond that stale (column “Status” under Individual sources). The overview shows the data age now – feed age at measurement plus time since the run – with one definition for tile, table and traffic light: current up to 30 minutes (collector interval 20 minutes plus 10), delayed up to 60 minutes, beyond that stale. Stale and time-unclear sources do not enter the figures but stay visible as a gap. Position age (per vehicle) and source age (per feed) are separate attributes.
app.numberFormatsAreNormalised: Number formats are normalised, clearly swapped latitudes and longitudes corrected. If a coordinate pair is missing, a referenced station position serves as a marked fallback. Positions outside Germany or without a municipality are left out. The municipality follows from GPS and the BKG municipal boundary (VG250, simplified approx. 30 m); one aggregate feed can serve several places. The operator selection follows the actual GPS coverage of the chosen place.
app.vehiclesOfSameOperatorAre: Vehicles of the same operator are merged across all sources: UUIDs and source prefixes are unified, the latest state wins, on a tie the direct position beats the station fallback. Identical IDs at distant positions (over 300 m) are kept as cases to check. Stations count as identical with the same ID or the same name within 60 m. A fingerprint of endpoint, version, feeds and vehicle types detects source changes; after that, time comparisons start over.
app.lowEnergyFollowsSameRule: “Low energy” follows the same rule everywhere as Operations: charge below 20 % and range below 5 km where a feed reports both; if it reports only one, that one decides. Operators that report range only (Lime) count by range below 5 km; their charge derived from range ÷ maximum range does not count. Denominators are the vehicles with energy data, disabled ones included; counting is per vehicle from the collector snapshot (or the live fetch). Alerts from 30 % low energy are graded by the deviation from the mean of previous days (otherwise of the day so far), measured on the charge share the daily values carry: from 5 points above notable, from 15 critical, a permanently high share stays a note. Thresholds can be set under Market view › Performance and apply to the live fetch; the collector uses 20 % and 5 km.
app.collectorRunsEvery20Minutes: The collector runs every 20 minutes independently of the browser (GitHub Actions) and stores cleaned totals per municipality, operator and vehicle type for 30 days. Individual vehicle paths are not archived. The live fetch in the browser reads the open feeds directly; access-restricted sources (MOBIDROM NRW) come as a snapshot of the last collector run. Δ collector compares the live state with the last collector point of the same source fingerprint.
app.sourceSQualityScoreRates: A source's quality score rates freshness (70 %) and available attributes such as energy, timestamps and vehicle type (30 %). It rates the source, not the company's operations. Disabled vehicles, empty stations and low batteries are hints from the feed; what an operator is working on right now is not known without internal access.
app.forEachVehicleCollectorKeeps: For each vehicle the collector keeps a hashed ID with rounded position, charge and disabled status. If an ID disappears between two runs, this counts as a trip start (for a disabled or nearly empty vehicle as a pickup); a new ID counts as a trip end. GBFS requires IDs to rotate after every trip, so these are counts without linking start to destination. For systems with stable IDs (such as station-based bikes) the ID returns; then duration and straight-line distance are measurable and shown as averages.
app.tripsTripsAreDerivedFrom: Trips. Trips are derived from consecutive collector runs (≈ 18 min). Disappeared and new IDs of an operator are paired globally by distance and charge: same charge (± 2 percentage points) up to 100 m, without charge up to 40 m is an ID rotation; a jump from < 40 to ≥ 85 % at the spot is a battery swap – neither is a trip. With stable IDs, a displacement ≥ 150 m is a trip if straight line / run interval gives 3.5–24 km/h (otherwise counted separately), except for collective transport (≥ 3 arrivals ≤ 40 m), disabling or ≥ 2 km without charge loss. Runs after gaps > 45 min do not count (after Xu et al. 2020; charge matching after Das & Nicklas 2026). Hours with such a run are grey in the daily profile and do not enter the extrapolation and trips/veh./day. Since 13 Nov 2026 each run's observation window counts pro rata in the clock hours it covers; before, it fell entirely into the hour in which the run ended (50–67 instead of 60 minutes per hour), and the extrapolation was about 7 % too high in the median. Since 13 Nov 2026 every published hour per operator holds 0 or at least 3 events; smaller amounts sit in an hour of the same time-of-day band, otherwise as a daily value without hour (daily total unchanged).
app.chargeJumpsFromBelow40ToAt: Charge jumps from below 40 % to at least 85 % at the same spot: battery swap; the waiting time measures the time below 20 % until the swap. Idle time is the time since the last position change over 50 m (at most since the first collector contact). Source outages create no trips. All values are estimates from 20-minute snapshots, not operator figures.
app.startAndDestinationCellsAre: Start and destination cells ({CELL}) are counted per municipality and day; “served” is a cell in which an available vehicle stood within 7 days. Operating zones come from geofencing_zones.json of the operator feeds, prices from system_pricing_plans.json; both are re-read on every run. Weather comes hourly from the collector's weather cache (DWD via Bright Sky) for the municipality's weather cell. Station availability rates count runs of the last 7 days in which a renting station had no bookable vehicle or no free dock.
app.ifSystemInCatalogueHasSecond: If a system in the catalogue has a second address (state feed and operator feed or two GBFS versions), the collector reads both and compares fleet, ID overlap (shared ÷ all IDs) and the median distance of identical IDs; if a directory re-keys the IDs (state feeds do), the share of vehicles with a vehicle of the other source within 10 m counts instead. If two sources of the same operator deliver vehicles in the same municipality, they are compared pairwise in the same way; “separate fleets” means the IDs hardly overlap. Walking routes in the stop analysis come from the pedestrian profile of the FOSSGIS routing services (Valhalla, on failure OSRM on routing.openstreetmap.de); per stop the two nearest vehicles are routed, the detour factor is walking route ÷ straight line.
app.estimatesAreAlignedWith: Estimates follow official reference values (data/reference.json); measured values are always shown alongside. Trip duration: The avg. trip of an e-scooter is the mean of the Berlin quarterly values Q1/2025–Q1/2026 (Abgeordnetenhaus Berlin, Vorgang h19-2915: 7.3 · 8.0 · 7.4 · 6.4 · 6.5 min, avg. 7.1 min and 1.5 km) instead of a flat 12 min; the Heilbronn Dott data (arXiv 2606.25484: median 6.9, mean 8.7 min) serve as a cross-check. Measured duration (20-min grid) applies only if it is lower. For bikes, e-bikes and cargo bikes there is no official evidence; the previous assumptions apply there. Trips: Chained trips swallowed between two fetches and ID rotation make the measurement too low. The method factor k is the official Berlin value of trips per e-scooter and day in the matching quarter (same quarter, otherwise the same calendar quarter of the previous year, otherwise the latest) divided by our Berlin measurement over the last up to 14 daily files. k applies to e-scooters nationwide and is shown as “calibrated (Berlin Qn/YYYY)”; the range follows from the smallest and largest Berlin quarterly value. Below 7 measurement days or below 50 % of observed hours of the day, k is preliminary; without a Berlin measurement there is no calibration. An own “Correction ×” replaces k per operator. Plausibility: If an operator's measured trips per e-scooter and day in an area exceed 1.5 times the largest Berlin quarterly value (2.31 × 1.5 ≈ 3.5), it counts as an overcount: calibration suspended, row not in totals. k comes only from Berlin operators with a plausible measurement; which ones is stated at the factor (currently only Dott, a limitation). Coverage: Own e-scooters ÷ official fleet – in Berlin the share of the licensed fleet (46,450 licensed vehicles as of 01/04/2026; lower bound of feed coverage, because not all licensed vehicles are on the street), in Munich of the active fleet (around 21,000 active, as of 04/11/2025; Munich issues no licences) – shows which part of the market is in open feeds; an extrapolation to the official fleet appears only in the “Calibration” panel. Check values without a factor: Frankfurt (10.49 m trips 2025 ÷ 365 ÷ fleet cap 12,000 ≈ 2.4 as a lower bound if the fleet respects the cap), Europe 1.6 (Fluctuo 2024) and the Voi group (2.40 trips and €3.64 revenue per vehicle and day in Q4/2025, all markets, incl. e-bikes).
app.openFeedsDoNotCoverAll: The open feeds do not cover all operators; shares always refer to the recorded vehicles. The net balance over ten minutes measures build-up or decline of the available fleet; rentals, returns, reservations and rebalancing have the same effect, a trip count cannot be derived from it. Supply distances are straight lines unless walking-route routing is enabled. Base map © OpenStreetMap contributors; stops from OpenStreetMap (ODbL).
